US-119-S240.title: Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025
US-119-S240.summary:
Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Amendments Act of 2025

This bill revises the water rights settlement agreement entered into by the Crow Tribe of Montana and Montana.

The Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010 ratified, authorized, and confirmed the water rights compact between the tribe and Montana. Among other provisions, this settlement act authorized the Bureau of Reclamation to plan, design and construct the following two major projects on the Crow Reservation: (1) the rehabilitation and improvement of the Crow Irrigation Project (CIP); and (2) the planning, design, and construction of the MR&I System (the municipal, rural, and industrial water system of the Crow Reservation).

Among other provisions, the bill revises the settlement act to
• replace references to the MR&I System with MR&I Projects ;
• establish a nontrust, interest-bearing account (to be known as the Crow CIP Implementation Account) to allow Reclamation to continue to work on the rehabilitation of the CIP;
• create a new MR&I Projects Account, through which the tribe must use funds for activities related to water production, treatment, or delivery infrastructure; and
• extend by five years (to 2030) the period during which the tribe has the exclusive right to construct hydropower facilities on the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam in Montana.

US-119-S240.aiSummary: This law updates a 2010 water rights settlement between the Crow Tribe of Montana and Montana. It changes how money is handled for the Crow Irrigation Project and for other water system projects tied to water supply, treatment, and delivery. It also extends the tribe’s exclusive right to build hydropower facilities on the Yellowtail Afterbay Dam to 2030.

US-119-HR10280.description: To provide for improvements in the implementation of the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10280.aiSummary: The bill would change how the national suicide prevention lifeline is run. It would add grants for local crisis call centers, fund a national suicide prevention media campaign, and provide money for health center building projects and crisis care sites. It would also change some Medicaid rules for crisis services.

US-119-HR9192.title: Prior Authorization Reform for Autoimmune and Blood Disorders Act

actions.text: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Education and Workforce, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
Introduced in House

US-119-HR9192.description: To amend the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, title XXVII of the Public Health Service Act, and the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to require health insurance coverage of drugs indicated for the treatment of autoimmune diseases and certain blood disorders.
US-119-HR9192.aiSummary: The bill would require certain health plans and insurers to cover drugs used to treat autoimmune diseases, hemophilia, and Von Willebrand disease. It would also limit how often a plan can require prior approval for those drugs to once in any 12-month period, with some exceptions. The changes would apply to plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.

US-119-S284.title: Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act
US-119-S284.summary:
Congressional Award Program Reauthorization Act

This act reauthorizes through FY2028 the Congressional Award Board, the board that administers the Congressional Award Program, and modifies program medals.

(The program, established by law in 1979, awards medals to youth ages 14 to 23 who satisfy standards of achievement set by the board. The program aims to promote initiative, achievement, and excellence among youth in the areas of public service, personal development, and physical fitness.)

The act removes a requirement for program medals to consist of gold-plate over bronze, rhodium over bronze, or bronze.

The reauthorization is effective as if enacted on October 1, 2023 (the date on which a prior reauthorization expired).
